solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Refusing to give in the end natural

parts.note: a stub is the short end left of a pencil or cigarette
born, as in 'a born leader', means natural

explanation.surface: Someone holding out to the very end, as if it were simply their nature.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate person will not yield, so refusing to give in describes them exactly.

clue.text: Ferries go so far and do not interfere with each other

indicators.note: letters that interfere with each other get mixed together, so the words far and do not are scrambled

explanation.surface: Ferries travel only so far and keep out of each other's way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Ferries go so', meaning the way ferries go: back and forth. 'interfere with each other' mixes the letters of FAR and DO NOT, and 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferries shuttle back and forth between two ports, which is the motion the phrase describes.

clue.text: Shift working interrupted by large strike

indicators.note: something interrupted by another thing has it break in, so the large letter goes inside

parts.note: to budge is to shift or move slightly
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A work shift broken off by a big strike, as in industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: To club someone heavily is to hit them, so the verb strike fits.

clue.text: Detective goes after taking too many chances

indicators.note: goes after places the detective letters behind the other piece

parts.note: OD means to overdose, taking too many pills
DS is a Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A detective who keeps taking too many risks.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting odds express the likelihood of an outcome, so they are the chances of it.

clue.text: Dancer's very visual awareness directed upwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, upwards means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an eye, as in 'an eye for detail', is visual awareness
to run something is to direct or manage it

explanation.surface: A dancer whose keen eye is always turned towards the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link. 'upwards' reverses V + EYE + RUN to read from the bottom of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was the celebrated Soviet-born ballet star who defected to the West in 1961.

clue.text: Psychologist fellow mistreated bird

parts.note: Carl Jung was the Swiss founder of analytical psychology

indicators.note: mistreated means the letters of fellow are handled roughly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A psychologist's colleague cruelly treated a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The red junglefowl of South-East Asia is the wild ancestor of the domestic chicken, a bird.

clue.text: Some empty praise offered up for one that's been let down?

indicators.note: some says only part of the praise word is turned, here its final three letters
in a down entry, offered up means that part of the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: flattery is insincere, empty praise

explanation.surface: Hollow compliments delivered to someone who has just been disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' and 'offered up' turn round only the last three letters of FLATTERY: ERY becomes YRE. 'let down' looks like disappointment but means deflated, as with air.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctured tyre has had its air let out, so it is literally something let down.

clue.text: Fugitives better stopping close to trouble spots

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of trouble
stopping means plugging a gap, so the better piece sits inside the others

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
to cap is to better or outdo, as in capping a joke

explanation.surface: Runaways do better by staying near the trouble spots.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have broken out of prison are on the run, so they are fugitives.

clue.text: Items plucked from French article repeatedly probing transatlantic allies

indicators.note: probing means pushing inside, so the repeated article goes within the allies

parts.note: UK and US are allies on either side of the Atlantic

indicators.note: repeatedly means the article is written twice

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: Things taken from a French newspaper article, repeatedly probing the British and American alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Small four-stringed Hawaiian guitars are played by plucking, so they are items plucked.

clue.text: Person looking round briefly to annul or lower offer

indicators.note: round says the looker's letters wrap around the shortened word

parts.note: a gazer is someone who looks or stares

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to undo something is to annul it

explanation.surface: Someone scanning the market briefly, aiming to cancel or reduce a bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops a final letter. Gazundering is the British house-buying practice of cutting your offer just before contracts are exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To gazunder is to lower one's bid for a property at the last minute, so it means lower offer.

clue.text: Taxi sent with gear as a favour

indicators.note: sent here means dispatched in disarray, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cab dispatched with your luggage, done as a kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex gratia payment is made voluntarily, without legal obligation, so it is given as a favour.

clue.text: A bit of late drama as pacifist is speaking out?

indicators.note: speaking out means the words are said aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a pacifist is someone who is after peace, seeking it

explanation.surface: A pacifist delivering a late dramatic speech.
explanation.walkthrough: A pacifist is someone 'after peace', and said aloud that phrase gives the theatre term. 'as' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A short play or farce staged after the main play of the evening is a late bit of drama.

clue.text: Relish film about boxer, badly brought up

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
c is circa, about
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A biopic of a boxer who was poorly raised.
explanation.definitionFit: This mustard-yellow pickle of chopped vegetables is a condiment, which is a relish.

clue.text: Ditch cheeky Dadaist exhibits, upon reflection

indicators.note: upon reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
exhibits says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An impudent avant-garde artist shows a ditch, after some thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A dike or dyke can be a channel dug for drainage, which is a ditch.

clue.text: Projecting course with appreciative exclamation

definitions.meaning: a moulded band of stone or plaster that juts out along the top of a wall or building
a British cry of delight, run together as two words: 'gosh, lovely!'

explanation.surface: A projecting architectural layer greeted with an approving cry.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise, so COR NICE! is a cry of approval. A course in building is one horizontal layer of brick or stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The architectural moulding is a horizontal layer that projects from a wall's top, and split in two the word is a delighted cry.

clue.text: Visible split in chest, or short split in coop

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the coop

parts.note: a coop is a cage for poultry

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to split is to leave, as in 'let's split'

explanation.surface: A crack showing in a chest, or a small split in a hen coop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' changes sense: the second one is slang for leave, and 'short' cuts it to LEAV.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible gap between a woman's breasts in a low-cut top is a divide on the chest.

clue.text: Lemur's call when encountering shadow

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
to tail is to follow or shadow someone

explanation.surface: A lemur's cry when it meets its own shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has' or 'is', a link; 'when encountering' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring-tailed lemur of Madagascar, with its banded tail, is called by this name.

clue.text: Quickly, for one round, the three of spades is played

indicators.note: is played means the letters are put into play and rearranged

parts.note: O is round in shape
three of spades read literally is three letters S, S being the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A card game: the three of spades is laid down quickly, for one round.
explanation.walkthrough: Mistress Quickly is the tavern landlady in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays, so she is an example of the answer. 'Quickly' looks like an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Quickly runs the Boar's Head inn, making her a landlady, an example of a woman who receives guests.

clue.text: Needleworker cheers dry reaction to double entendre?

parts.note: ta is British for thanks, cheers
TT is teetotal, abstaining from drink, dry
ooer is a camp British exclamation at an unintended rude meaning

explanation.surface: A seamstress responds with thanks, abstinence and a smirk at innuendo.
explanation.walkthrough: OOER is a British comic response to a smutty double meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who inks designs into skin works with a needle, a punning needleworker.

clue.text: Paraded with a Yankee, in a band, all round

indicators.note: all round means the band piece surrounds the other letters

parts.note: sashed means wearing a sash, a band of cloth
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American marched with a band, all the way round.
explanation.walkthrough: A and Y go inside SASHED after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a showy, swaggering way, so it is to strut or parade.

clue.text: It is a cat mostly mistaken for a type of lion

indicators.note: mistaken means the letters are got wrong and jumbled
mostly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A cat that is usually confused with a kind of lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts cat to CA, and 'mistaken' rearranges ITISA + CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asiatic lion, found in India's Gir Forest, is a subspecies of lion.

clue.text: Bird to take home picked up from trap?

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so words picked up from it are heard aloud

parts.note: to earn is to take home pay

explanation.surface: A bird that has been taken home after being caught in a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' looks like a snare for the bird but is slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite, is a bird.

clue.text: Despot employing muscle, hence someone pulling the strings?

parts.note: ab is short for an abdominal muscle
so means therefore, hence
a lutist plucks the strings of a lute; the question mark flags the play on puppetry

explanation.surface: A tyrant who uses force, and so controls everything from behind the scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolutist upholds absolute, unrestricted power, so a ruler of that kind is a despot.

clue.text: Checking short cuts using vision aid

indicators.note: cuts means the shortened word slices into the other piece

parts.note: via means by way of, using

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taming a wild thing is checking or curbing it

explanation.surface: An eye test where shortcuts are taken with the vision aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinol is needed for the retina to work in dim light, so it is a nutrient that aids vision.

clue.text: Case for English port

definitions.meaning: an outer covering, like the husk or shell of a seed or pod
the Yorkshire city on the Humber estuary in north-east England

explanation.surface: Luggage destined for an English harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod's husk is its outer covering, and Kingston upon Hull is a major port on England's east coast.

clue.text: Pulled — hard — leg of the setter about taxonomic term

parts.note: a rope pulled hard is taut
in cricket, the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the setter's word is read backwards

parts.note: of the setter means belonging to me, my

explanation.surface: The setter, pulling hard on a leg, about a scientific naming term.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side of a cricket field is also the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientific name whose genus and species parts are the same, like Gorilla gorilla, is a term used in taxonomy.

clue.text: Old pantomime actor threatening odd couples in Aladdin

parts.note: grim means forbidding or threatening

indicators.note: odd couples means the first and third pairs of letters of Aladdin are kept, dropping the rest

explanation.surface: A menacing old pantomime performer with a strange couple of parts in Aladdin.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Aladdin into pairs AL, AD, DI and N; the odd ones, first and third, give ALDI. Aladdin is a classic British Christmas pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Grimaldi was the great Regency clown of English pantomime, so he is an old pantomime actor.

clue.text: Depression and fuss, with men getting in a state

indicators.note: getting in means the men go inside the other pieces

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks
ado means fuss or bother
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Low spirits and a commotion as the men work themselves into a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty constituent parts of the USA, so it is a state.
